jobs.title: Helpers
jobs.description:
Key responsibilities
Assist authorized PMU personnel with routine logistical support, movement and orderly stacking of non-hazardous supplies, furniture and project materials.
Assist with physical receipt, counting, labelling, movement and storage of supplies under supervision.
Assist in preparing meeting venues, field visit logistics, temporary work areas and non-technical site arrangements.
Maintain cleanliness and basic order in assigned storage and work areas; Ensure proper collection and disposal of waste and promptly report any unsafe or hazardous conditions to the immediate supervisor.
Assist skilled technical staff only with basic non-electrical, non-specialist tasks under direct supervision and applicable safety instructions.
Do not operate electrical systems, solar PV equipment, lifting machinery, vehicles or hazardous tools unless separately trained and expressly authorized.
Follow PPE, manual-handling, fire-safety and weather-related precautions; promptly report injuries, damage and safety hazards.
Maintain accountability for tools and materials issued for work; report loss or damage immediately.
Perform other lawful general support duties assigned by authorized supervisor.
Minimum eligibility
Qualification: Primary/Middle education preferred; ability to understand safety instructions and undertake routine manual support tasks. Ability of reading/writing basic Urdu/English preferred.
Experience: At least 3 years of relevant experience in site support, store handling, general maintenance assistance or project logistics preferred.
Age: 35 years.

jobs.title: Chowkidars
jobs.description:
Key responsibilities
Provide watch-and-ward coverage of assigned PMU office, store or approved project premises according to authorized shifts and duty roster.
Monitor entrances and exits, verify visitor authorization and maintain visitor and incident registers as instructed.
Conduct periodic perimeter and premises checks and report suspicious activity, damaged locks, fire risks, water leakage or unauthorized access.
Safeguard doors, gates, lights and designated property during assigned shifts; ensure secure handover of keys and security instructions.
Immediately inform supervisor and relevant emergency services of security incidents, theft, fire or medical emergencies.
Coordinate with authorized police, building security and local administration through designated PMU officers when required.
Maintain shift handover notes, incident reports and attendance records; remain on duty until properly relieved.
Treat all staff and visitors respectfully and preserve confidentiality of site operations and official information.
Perform other lawful watch-and-ward duties assigned by authorized supervisor.
Minimum eligibility
Qualification: Primary/Middle education with ability to maintain simple entries or verbal handover. Matriculation with the ability of reading/writing basic Urdu/English preferred.
Experience: At least 3 years of relevant watch-and-ward/security experience preferred; experience at government/project premises advantageous.
Age: 35 years.

jobs.title: Office Boys
jobs.description:
Key responsibilities
Provide day-to-day office assistance including movement of files, official correspondence, photocopying, scanning, printing and delivery of documents within authorized offices.
Arrange meeting rooms, seating, water, refreshments and basic stationery for official meetings and visitors.
Assist with receiving, sorting and dispatching mail and maintain acknowledgment/dispatch records as instructed.
Assist in orderly storage and authorized distribution of stationery and office supplies; report shortages and faults.
Keep assigned workstations and common office areas orderly and assist with light non-hazardous housekeeping tasks.
Handle confidential documents carefully; do not disclose, photograph or remove records without authorization.
Assist administrative staff with routine clerical support appropriate to the post and with approved movement of light office materials (e.g. office files, stationery, paper bundles, small office supplies and lightweight equipment etc).
Observe office timings, discipline, courteous conduct and health and safety instructions.
Perform other lawful office-support duties assigned by authorized supervisor.
Minimum eligibility
Qualification: Primary/Middle pass; Should be capable of reading/writing basic Urdu/English.
Experience: At least 3 years of relevant office-support experience.
Age: 35 years.

jobs.title: Driver
jobs.description:
Key responsibilities
Drive authorized PMU personnel and transport official documents/material to approved offices and project sites safely and punctually.
Operate vehicles in accordance with traffic laws, approved travel instructions and road/weather conditions; exercise particular care on mountainous roads.
Conduct daily pre-trip checks of tyres, brakes, lights, fluids, emergency equipment and vehicle roadworthiness; report defects without delay.
Maintain accurate trip, mileage and fuel-consumption logbooks and submit supporting operational records to Administration.
Keep the assigned vehicle clean, secure and roadworthy; report servicing and repair needs to Administration and assist with vehicle inspection and fitness documentation.
Do not permit unauthorized passengers, personal use or unsafe overloading; safeguard keys and vehicle documents.
Assist with loading/unloading official materials when safe and appropriate; observe confidentiality regarding official travel and documents.
Immediately report accidents, breakdowns, security concerns and near misses; follow emergency instructions.
Perform other lawful transport-related duties assigned by authorized PMU management.
Minimum eligibility
Qualification: Matric pass; valid driving license; ability to maintain basic trip records. Should have the ability to drive different kinds of vehicles and motorcycles with basic technical knowledge of petrol/diesel vehicles.
Experience: At least 5 years of verifiable driving experience, preferably in mountainous terrain and government/development projects.
Age: 40 years.

jobs.title: Accountant & Cashier
jobs.description:
Role purpose
Manage PMU-Solar accounting records, budget utilization, financial documentation and controlled cash/banking transactions in accordance with authorized government/PPIB financial procedures.
Key responsibilities
Maintain project accounting ledgers, expenditure records, cash/petty-cash books, bank/assignment-account documentation and periodic reconciliations in accordance with applicable financial rules and approved procedures.
Track approved PSDP releases, budget allocations, commitments, advances, liabilities and expenditures and prepare financial utilization and management reports.
Assist in reconciling historical solar-component expenditures and advances transferred from W&PD GB, with supporting source records and audit trails.
Check completeness of EPC/consultancy invoices, consultant/TPV milestones and financial documents before forwarding them through the designated verification and payment approval channels.
Process authorized payroll, allowances, office expenses and other approved payments, and maintain vouchers, tax withholding records and relevant financial registers.
Support internal/external audit, financial reporting and statutory/tax compliance. Do not approve, certify and disburse the same transaction without the required independent checks.
Minimum eligibility
Qualification: EITHER (a) a 16-year HEC-recognized degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce or Business Administration (Finance); OR (b) a HEC-recognized B.Com/equivalent 14-year commerce/accounting qualification together with the longer relevant experience specified below.
Experience: For applicants with a 16-year degree: at least 5 years of relevant post-qualification experience. For applicants with a 14-year B.Com/equivalent: at least 7 years of relevant post-qualification experience. Experience must be in accounting, project/government finance, banking/reconciliations, budgets or audit-related financial administration. Should possess practical proficiency in ledgers, bank/cash reconciliation, payment vouchers, supporting documents, MS Excel, applicable withholding taxes and financial reporting.
Preferred Experience: Public-sector finance, PSDP releases, assignment-account operations, AGPR procedures, EPC invoice handling or audit compliance is desirable.
Age: 30 years.

jobs.title: Manager Administration
jobs.description:
Role purpose
Manage PMU-Solar administrative operations, personnel support, logistics and office facilities at PPIB headquarters and approved GB field offices, under delegated PPIB procedures.
Key responsibilities
Establish and administer the approved PMU office arrangements, including premises, utilities, communications, inventory, recordkeeping and office services.
Manage personnel files, attendance/leave records, staff deployment and travel logistics, and support recruitment, performance appraisal and contract administration through authorized HR channels.
Coordinate procurement requisitions, office equipment, vehicle allocation and maintenance, fleet logs, fuel controls and administrative vendor services under applicable rules.
Arrange site visits, inspections, meetings and official travel.
Maintain asset and document-control registers, physical/electronic records, official correspondence and administrative performance reports.
Coordinate office security, employee safety and business continuity with project management and relevant local authorities.
Minimum eligibility
Qualification: Minimum 16 years of education in Business Administration, Public Administration, Management Sciences, Human Resource Management or Commerce from an HEC-recognized university.
Experience: At least 8 years of relevant post-qualification experience in office administration, HR, logistics, facilities or fleet/asset management, preferably including experience supporting field offices or project teams. Must possess ability to manage administrative documentation, HR/attendance records, procurements/requisitions, inventories, travel and field logistics, office systems and formal correspondence.
Preferred Experience: Public-sector/PSDP project administration, procurement procedures, GB logistics and government/autonomous-body experience are desirable.
Age: 35 years.

jobs.title: Chief Software Architect
jobs.description:
Role purpose
The Chief Software Architect will provide strategic leadership for PDA’s software architecture and engineering direction, supporting the delivery of secure, scalable and interoperable digital platforms and government services. The role will translate the National Digital Masterplan and institutional requirements into software architecture standards, reusable capabilities and modernisation roadmaps.
Combining a strong software development background with executive leadership, the Chief Software Architect will guide critical technology decisions, strengthen engineering capability and oversee architectural quality across PDA-supported programmes.
Key responsibilities
Define and lead PDA’s software architecture strategy, aligning technology decisions with national digital priorities, service needs and delivery outcomes.
Establish reference architectures, software design standards and reusable patterns that support interoperability and consistent implementation across government programmes.
Lead application modernisation strategy, assessing legacy systems and defining practical roadmaps for migration, integration, replacement or retirement.
Guide the adoption of cloud-native architectures, APIs, microservices and other technologies where they meet business, operational and sustainability requirements.
Establish architecture governance and design assurance, working with the Architecture Review Board and relevant technology leaders to review major designs, resolve exceptions and manage technical debt.
Ensure software solutions address security, privacy, accessibility, resilience, performance and maintainability from design through operation.
Partner with DPI, data, AI, cybersecurity, product and delivery leaders to align software architecture with shared platforms and end-to-end service requirements.
Evaluate major technology investments and supplier proposals, considering technical suitability, lifecycle costs, portability, vendor dependency and knowledge transfer.
Strengthen software engineering practices, including secure development, automated testing, DevSecOps, release assurance and operational readiness.
Build and mentor architecture and engineering capability, providing technical direction to internal teams and delivery partners.
Advise the Chairperson and senior leadership on software strategy, emerging technologies, delivery risks and significant architectural decisions.
Qualifications and experience
Bachelor’s in Computer Science, Software

Define data ownership and stewardship arrangements, classification, quality, metadata, lineage, retention and lifecycle standards, with clear responsibilities and assurance measures.
Coordinate with ministries, provinces, regulators and data custodians to enable secure data sharing and resolve barriers to interoperability and adoption.
Work with DPI and Technology leaders on data exchange requirements, reference architectures and shared registries; retain focus on governance and stewardship responsibilities.
Develop proposals for open data, controlled access, sensitive data handling and cross-border arrangements with Legal, Security and relevant authorities, subject to applicable requirements and approvals.
Work in partnership with the AI Office on data readiness, provenance, quality and appropriate use of datasets supporting AI systems.
Build the Data governance team and institutional capability; establish maturity assessments, adoption measures and reporting on data quality and governance risks.

Evidence of establishing and embedding data governance across multiple business units, institutions or jurisdictions, with measurable improvements in data quality, sharing or use.
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and advising executive decision-makers on data policy, investment, privacy and operational trade-offs.

jobs.title: Chief Product Officer
jobs.description:
Role Purpose
Lead the strategy, prioritisation and performance of the digital product portfolio assigned to PDA. Build a product management capability that converts policy priorities and citizen needs into secure, accessible services, working with responsible government service owners and PDA’s design, technology and delivery functions.
Key responsibilities
Develop the assigned product portfolio strategy and investment priorities in alignment with the National Digital Masterplan, public value and available delivery capacity.
Lead product discovery, business cases, roadmaps and lifecycle decisions from initial concept through launch, improvement and retirement, within approved decision rights.
Establish product outcomes and measures covering adoption, task completion, service quality, accessibility, reliability and cost-effectiveness; use evidence to guide investment.
